**RE: Appeal of Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18**

- **Member name:** Skyler Iverson
- **Member ID:** W313340363
- **Reference number:** POC-30230D15F4-69823
- **Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan:** Medicaid (Medicaid), State of Alaska

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551, which the plan denied in its notice dated 2026-08-18, reference number POC-30230D15F4-69823. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery my surgeon has documented that I need.

**A note about the criteria used to deny my request.** The notice states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not name that policy or set out any of its language, and no policy language has been provided to me. Because of that, I am not able to quote the plan's own criteria back to it in this letter, and I am not going to guess at what those criteria say. I am making my argument from the facts in my medical records instead. I ask the plan to keep in mind, in reviewing this appeal, that I have not been shown the standard my request was measured against.

## Request for the criteria in writing

I am requesting, in writing, a copy of the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization — the specific medical policy, guideline, or vendor criteria set the reviewer used to decide that CPT 22551 was not medically necessary for me, including any imaging thresholds or findings it requires. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. I am also requesting the name and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination. I am sending a copy of this request to the Alaska state Medicaid agency. I ask that the criteria be sent to me at the address above, and that I be given a reasonable opportunity to respond to them before a final decision is made on this appeal.

## The reason given for the denial, and what my records actually show

The stated reason for the denial is that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. My records show the following, and I ask that each point be checked against whatever criteria the plan applied:

**The imaging identifies a specific structural problem at a specific level.** An MRI of my cervical spine on 2026-06-28 showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This is not a general or vague finding. It names the level, the side, and the nerve root involved.

**My symptoms and my physical exam match that imaging.** I have radicular pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger, with weakness. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The imaging finding and the clinical findings point to the same nerve root on the same side. This correlation is the central point of my appeal: the images are not being read in isolation, and they line up with what my body is doing.

**My symptoms have been going on a long time and are getting worse.** I have had 12 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest.

**I have tried non-surgical treatment first, and it is documented.** I completed supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training over 8 weeks, from 2026-05-06 to 2026-07-01, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-06, which gave me only 3 weeks of partial relief.

**I am an appropriate surgical candidate.** My records show no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

My surgeon, Okafor, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed. The prior authorization packet contains imaging that identifies the lesion, an examination that confirms it at the same level, a year of worsening symptoms, and a full course of conservative care that did not work. If the plan's criteria call for imaging that corresponds to the patient's clinical findings, my records establish that. If the plan's criteria call for documented failure of conservative treatment before surgery, my records establish that as well.

## What I am asking for

I ask the plan to:

1. Overturn the denial and approve CPT 22551 as requested by Okafor, MD;
2. Send me, in writing, the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization, as requested above; and
3. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, tell me in writing exactly which criterion my records did not meet and what specific documentation would satisfy it.

I understand that this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14, which is 180 days from the date of the notice, and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I also understand that I may request a State Fair Hearing through the Alaska state Medicaid agency, and I reserve my right to do so. If anything further is needed from me or from my surgeon's office, please contact me at the phone number above.

I am enclosing the following records in support of this appeal:

- [MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-28]
- [Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-06 to 2026-07-01, 20 visits]
- [Office notes from Okafor, MD, including examination findings]
- [Injection record dated 2026-05-06]
- [Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18]

Thank you for taking the time to review this carefully.

Sincerely,

 

_________________________
**Skyler Iverson**

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
